> **Design update 2026-10-16 (the Epic 11 header; DS rounds 1–3):** some verbs now return jj's hints as data, because the UI shows them verbatim (decision 16.25). This note amends item 2 and the non-goal "no hint porting". It adds no items and no witnesses.
> - **Item 2 and Non-goals.** "Hints are not ported" stays for this story's warnings. Hints that a UI shows verbatim travel as plan or result data of their verb: 9.20 items 3, 4 and 8, 9.21 item 3, and the undo-push hint "To avoid this, run `jj redo` now." behind 10.23's Redo (undo.rs:140 @ v0.46.0).

**Motivation.** Zanshin already answers refusals with a machine-readable code (`Envelope.error { code, context }`, registry `docs/rust-error-codes.md`), but it has no uniform channel for the other half of what the CLI prints: **success with a warning**. Today each such fact is a one-off field — `MutationResult.identity_missing` (9.27), `Precondition.working_copy_immutable_new_commit` and `Precondition.jjconflict_files_present` (9.26) — and the creation verbs cannot report anything at all (9.33). Ralph's idea (2026-09-24): a status with a code the UI can switch on, so Zanshin can offer the remedy itself (missing identity → "set your identity") without ever parsing text. Decided shape: a **list** of warnings next to the existing result, not one HTTP-style status per response, because several warnings can hold at once (a clone with an empty identity AND a file too large to track AND a failed ref export).

**Scope (backend + bridge).**
1. **Wire:** `Envelope.warnings: [Warning]` (appended field, WIP in-place edit), `table Warning { code: string; message: string; }`. Present on ok AND error envelopes (a precondition that wrote operations before the verb refused still warns). Success without caveat = `ok = true` and an empty list — there is no "success" code.
2. **Rule:** every warning the CLI @ v0.44.0 writes through `ui.warning_default()` (or another `ui.warning_*` writer) and emits on a code path Zanshin ports becomes ONE warning code. Status lines (`ui.status()`: "Nothing changed.", "Already editing that commit.") are NOT warnings — they stay typed facts (e.g. the unchanged op id). Hints (`ui.hint_*`) are not ported — the UI derives its offer from the code. First task: an inventory of the warning sites on every shipped verb's path (`workspace_helper`/`snapshot_impl`, `finish_transaction`, the verb bodies), each mapped to a code or recorded as out of scope with the reason.
3. **Codes** live in the same registry as the error codes (a new "Warning codes" section of `docs/rust-error-codes.md`), `jj.` namespace, one code per remedy (the house rule for errors) — e.g. `jj.identity_missing`, `jj.working_copy_immutable`, `jj.snapshot_files_refused`, `jj.jjconflict_files_present`, `jj.git_export_failed`. `message` = the CLI's text verbatim where it has one (log/tooltip only; the UI never parses it). Structured data stays typed where it already is (`SnapshotStats`, `GitExportResult`, …): the warning says that there is something, the payload says what.
4. **One mechanism:** `MutationResult.identity_missing`, `Precondition.working_copy_immutable_new_commit` and `Precondition.jjconflict_files_present` move into warnings and the fields are removed (WIP in-place edit; the UI does not consume them yet). Which `FinishFacts` fields are warnings and which are data is part of the inventory.
5. **Rust surface:** the warnings leave `zanshin-jj` with the result they belong to (one collector per call, like `take_precondition()`), so MCP (Epic 7) inherits them.
6. **Dart:** every command's result exposes its warnings on success, handle-scoped and handle-less alike (the error path is 9.35); typed Dart constants for the registered codes.
7. `docs/ffi-abi.md` (envelope contract), coverage ratchet, a `zanshin_core` witness for every warning code a fixture can produce.

**Non-goals.** No UI (the "set your identity" offer is Ralph's); no severity levels beyond warning vs. error; no localization; no hint porting.

**Related:** 9.26 (`precondition`), 9.27 (`identity_missing`), 9.33, 9.35, 9.37 (secure-config warnings), 9.39 (undo-a-push warning), FR-JJ-17, AR-P-4.

### Story 9.33: Creation paths report what the CLI prints — `clone`/`init`/`convert`: `jj.identity_missing` + the conversion's snapshot report [M]
*(Added 2026-09-24, Ralph — decision "extend the return value" on the 9.27 and 9.26 follow-up deferrals. Depends on 9.32.)*

**Motivation.** The CLI warns about an empty identity in `finish_transaction`, which `jj git clone` reaches via `tx.finish(ui, "fetch from git remote into empty repo")` (`cli/src/commands/git/clone.rs:457` @ v0.44.0, also `:314`, `:352`) and `jj git init` over an existing Git repo via `tx.finish(ui, "import git head")` (`init.rs:268`). `zanshin_repo_clone`/`_init`/`_convert` return only a `RepoHandle`, so a GUI clone — the typical first action on a new machine — writes its operations and `@` with the empty identity and the UI learns of it only at the first later mutation. Likewise the conversion's snapshot (`maybe_snapshot` in `jj git init` over an existing repo) drops its report — files left untracked by `snapshot.max-new-file-size`/`auto-track`, the colocated `.jjconflict` warning, export and HEAD-reset failures — because 9.26's AC-3 kept `precondition` off convert envelopes.

**Scope.** (1) The three creation envelopes carry 9.32's warnings exactly where the CLI's flow warns: `jj.identity_missing` only when a `finish_transaction`-equivalent committed an operation (verify each flow @ v0.44.0 — a fresh `init` of an empty directory finishes no transaction, so no warning), plus the conversion's snapshot/export warnings. (2) The conversion's snapshot report rides the convert envelope as the `Precondition`/`SnapshotStats` data 9.26 defined (AC-3's exclusion lifted). (3) Dart `clone`/`init`/`convert` return the handle together with warnings and report. (4) Witnesses per flow: clone with and without identity, init of an empty directory vs. over an existing Git repo, convert (colocated and import) with a file over the size limit.

**Non-goals.** No change to what the flows do (9.20 owns the remaining clone/init parity gaps); no UI.

### Story 9.34: Snapshot knobs read after `import git head` — the CLI's refusal order in the precondition [M]
*(Added 2026-09-24, Ralph — from the 9.26 deferral "Wrong-typed snapshot knob is refused BEFORE the head import". Direction: the CLI's order, per Ralph's parity rule.)*

**Motivation.** Zanshin's precondition reads `snapshot.auto-track`, `snapshot.max-new-file-size`, the ignore files and `immutable_heads()` before taking `git_import_export.lock` (`snapshot.rs::Knobs::read`, `repo.rs::Repo::precondition`); the CLI reads the snapshot knobs only inside `snapshot_working_copy`, i.e. after its lock and its `import git head` (`cli_util.rs::workspace_helper_with_stats` → `snapshot_impl` @ v0.44.0). Observable in the double fault "Git HEAD moved outside AND a wrong-typed snapshot knob": the CLI writes `import git head` and then fails, Zanshin writes nothing and fails — two different op logs. Pinned today by `tests/snapshot_colocated.rs::a_wrong_typed_knob_is_refused_before_the_lock`; the 9.26 matrix row "refused before the lock" was the spec's wording, not the CLI's behaviour.

**Scope.** Read each knob where the CLI reads it (snapshot knobs inside the snapshot step; `immutable_heads()` where `snapshot_working_copy` needs it); invert the pinning test into the CLI's sequence (`import git head` written, then `jj.config_error`); rework the lock-wait witness that relied on the early read; a dated note on the 9.26 spec's matrix row (the CLI wins).

**Non-goals.** No other precondition change.

### Story 9.35: Dart keeps `precondition` and `warnings` on error results — handle-less commands included [bridge]
*(Added 2026-09-24, Ralph — from the 9.28 deferral "`zanshin_config_set`'s precondition is dropped on the Dart ERROR path". Depends on 9.32.)*

**Motivation.** Rust stamps `Envelope.precondition` (9.26) — and after 9.32 `Envelope.warnings` — on error envelopes too: a verb whose precondition snapshotted or imported (and wrote operations) and then refused. The Dart decoders throw `ZanshinFfiException` with code and context only, and `ZanshinWorker.send` records `lastPrecondition` only for handle-scoped commands. So the UI loses the report exactly when something went wrong — e.g. a `config_set` of `user.name` whose identity snapshot ran and then hit `jj.config_would_overwrite`.

**Scope.** The Dart error result (`ZanshinFfiException` or its successor) carries the envelope's `precondition` and `warnings`; every decoder passes them through; handle-less commands (`config_*`, the creation verbs) expose them the same way as handle-scoped ones; a real-cdylib witness per command family that produces an error envelope with a precondition or a warning. Bridge-only unless an error path turns out not to stamp the envelope.

**Non-goals.** No UI.

### Story 9.36: Finder/Dock launch sees the login-shell environment — `JJ_CONFIG`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `JJ_*` as in the terminal [bootstrap]
*(Added 2026-09-24, Ralph — from the 9.27 deferral "A Finder/Dock-launched Zanshin does not see the user's shell environment". **Decided 2026-09-24, Ralph: option (a)** — resolve the login-shell environment at start-up; (b) and (c) are kept below for the record only.)*

**Motivation.** 9.27's stack reads `JJ_CONFIG`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `JJ_USER`/`JJ_EMAIL`/`JJ_OP_*`, `VISUAL`/`EDITOR` and `NO_COLOR` exactly as the CLI does (`config.rs::ConfigEnv::from_env`), but an app launched by launchd gets launchd's minimal environment, not the login shell's. A user who sets `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `JJ_CONFIG` in a shell rc file then gets a different config — and identity — in Zanshin than in the terminal `jj`; the same holds for what jj-lib's `git` subprocess sees on fetch/push (`PATH`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `GIT_*`). Started from a terminal Zanshin behaves like the CLI; started from Finder it does not.

**Options (decided: (a)).** (a) Resolve the login-shell environment once at start-up — spawn `$SHELL -l -i -c` with a machine-readable `env` dump and a timeout, the approach VS Code and other macOS developer GUIs use — and hand the result to the config stack and the git subprocess environment as an explicit map (never `std::env::set_var` in a running multi-threaded process); fall back to launchd's environment on timeout or failure and report that as a 9.32 warning. (b) Nothing in the backend; document that shell-only variables do not reach a Finder-launched Zanshin. (c) A Zanshin setting that names `JJ_CONFIG`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` explicitly. Recommendation: (a) — the only option under which the same user gets the same config in both tools without having to know about launchd.

**Scope.** The resolution in the app bootstrap before the worker isolate opens a repo (worker boot is bridge scope; the map crosses to Rust once at init); `ConfigEnv` and the git subprocess environment read that map instead of the process environment; tests with a fake `$SHELL`; the fallback warning.

**Non-goals.** No UI beyond the warning; no edits to shell rc files.

### Story 9.37: Secure-config fix-ups at every command start — `SecureConfig::maybe_load_config` parity (legacy `.jj/repo/config.toml` migration, moved/copied repos) [M]
*(Added 2026-09-24, Ralph — from the 9.28 deferral "Read-side secure-config fix-ups are still not run". Direction: reverse "reading never writes" per Ralph's parity rule, as 9.26 reversed D2.)*

**Motivation.** At the start of every command the CLI loads the repo and workspace config through `ConfigEnv::reload_repo_config` / `reload_workspace_config` → `SecureConfig::maybe_load_config` (`cli/src/config.rs:585-593`, `:653-665`, called from `cli_util.rs:4545-4549` and `:4592-4595` @ v0.44.0). That call migrates a legacy `.jj/repo/config.toml` into the secure config directory and re-points or copies the config of a moved or copied repo, printing its `warnings` via `ui.warning_default()`. Zanshin's read path never writes (`config.rs` module doc "Reading never writes"), so `config_list` shows the legacy path until a CLI run or a Zanshin config WRITE migrates it, and a moved or copied repo is not fixed up the way the CLI's next command fixes it. Every on-disk effect of the CLI is required parity.

**Scope.** Run `maybe_load_config` for repo and workspace where the CLI does: `Repo::open`, the settings refresh at every verb start (9.27's fingerprint path — the fix-up must not trigger a reload loop), and the handle-less `config_*` functions with a workspace root (9.28); its warnings become 9.32 warning codes; `config.rs`'s "Reading never writes" doc and the 9.28 deferral are updated. Witnesses: a legacy file is migrated on first open and then listed with its new path; a copied repo gets its own config on open (cf. the 9.28 follow-up's copied-repo allow-list fix); no second migration on the next verb. Note: the CLI's `default_config_migrations()` (key renames through `jj_lib::config::migrate`) is empty at v0.44.0 — re-check at every pin bump; rules added there belong to this story's mechanism.

**Non-goals.** No `config gc` change (9.28 ported it).

### Story 9.38: `edit` of the current `@` is a no-op — "Already editing that commit." parity [M]
*(Added 2026-09-24, Ralph — pre-existing divergence found by the 9.26 follow-up review.)*

**Motivation.** `cmd_edit` (`cli/src/commands/edit.rs` @ v0.44.0) resolves the revision, runs `check_rewritable`, and then — when `get_wc_commit_id() == Some(new_commit.id())` — prints "Already editing that commit." and opens NO transaction. Zanshin's `mutate.rs::edit` always commits `edit commit <id>`, so `jj op log` gains an entry the CLI never writes, and a CLI `jj undo` after a Zanshin no-op edit undoes the previous real operation instead.

**Scope.** The same early return after the immutability check and before the transaction, returning the house no-op result (`new_op_id` = the pre-call head); an immutable current `@` still refuses as `jj.immutable` (the CLI checks first); witnesses for both plus the unchanged op count. The implicit snapshot (9.26) still runs first, as in the CLI.

### Story 9.39: `undo` = the v0.44.0 undo stack — a repeated `undo` goes further back [M]
*(Added 2026-09-24, Ralph — pre-existing divergence found by the 9.26 follow-up review. Related to 9.21 (`redo`) and 9.40 (no-change gate).)*

**Motivation.** `op_log.rs::undo` is v0.42.0's single-step walk-back; its doc says a second undo redoes the first. v0.44.0's `cmd_undo` (`cli/src/commands/undo.rs`) grows an undo stack keyed on the description prefix `UNDO_OP_DESC_PREFIX = "undo: restore to operation "`: undoing an undo-operation undoes the operation that undo restored to (going further back); a restore target that is itself an undo resolves to the original operation (no linked list of undos); redo is the separate `jj redo` (9.21). Refusals: "Cannot undo root operation", "Cannot undo a merge operation" (hint: `jj op restore`); undoing a push warns "Undoing a push operation often leads to conflicted bookmarks." The restore is `view_with_desired_portions_restored(target_parent.view, base.view, &DEFAULT_REVERT_WHAT)` under the description `undo: restore to operation <hex>`. A user alternating between CLI and Zanshin gets different results from the second undo today.

**Scope.** Port the stack walk step for step (both prefix look-ups, the at-most-one-parent refusals, `DEFAULT_REVERT_WHAT`, the description); the push warning as a 9.32 warning code (`is_push_operation`); witnesses for the op-log example in the CLI's own comment (A, B, C, undo, E, undo, undo → A), the root and merge refusals, and CLI↔Zanshin interleaving (an undo stack started by one tool is continued by the other). An undo that restores a view equal to the current one writes nothing — that comes from 9.40's gate.

**Non-goals.** `jj redo` (9.21), `op restore` / `op revert` (9.12).

**Update 2026-10-08 (jj 0.46, done).** Ported against `cmd_undo` @ v0.46.0, which adds two things to the scope above: an operation performed in ANOTHER workspace is refused ("Refusing to undo operation … because it was performed in workspace …") unless `--allow-cross-workspace` — `Repo::undo(allow_cross_workspace)`, `jj.undo_cross_workspace`, the flag through the FFI and `zanshin_core`; and undoing a `remove workspace` operation warns like a push does (`jj.undo_workspace_removal`, next to `jj.undo_push_operation`).

### Story 9.40: No-change verbs write no operation — `WorkspaceCommandTransaction::finish`'s `has_changes()` gate [M]
*(Added 2026-09-24, Ralph — pre-existing divergence first found by the 9.27 review, re-found by the 9.26 follow-up review.)*

**Motivation.** Every CLI verb that ends in `tx.finish(ui, …)` goes through `WorkspaceCommandTransaction::finish` (`cli_util.rs:2790-2806` @ v0.44.0), which prints "Nothing changed." and commits NO operation when `!tx.repo().has_changes()` — and therefore also shows no identity warning. `mutate::finish_verb` ports that function without the gate, so a `describe` with the same text, a `git fetch` that brings nothing, and an `undo` that restores an identical view all write an operation the CLI never writes; 9.27's identity fact fires with it, and a CLI `jj undo` afterwards undoes the wrong operation. `describe` additionally drops unchanged commits before rewriting (`describe.rs`: `old_commit.description() != commit_builder.description()`), so no descendant is rebased.

**Scope.** Add the gate to `finish_verb` (no-op result = the pre-call head op id, the house contract); port `describe`'s unchanged-description filter; audit every `finish_verb` caller against its CLI verb (does the CLI reach `tx.finish`, or commit the raw transaction like `track`/`untrack`?); witnesses per verb (describe with the same text, fetch with nothing new, undo to an equal view; the verbs already routed through `finish_or_no_op` stay unchanged). Coordinate with 9.30's fetch rework — whichever lands first owns fetch's witness.

**Non-goals.** `edit`'s guard (9.38), the undo stack (9.39).

**Update 2026-10-08 (jj 0.46 bump).** The gate is unchanged at v0.46.0 — `WorkspaceCommandTransaction::finish` is now `cli_util.rs:2849-2865` ("Nothing changed." → no commit; descendants are rebased through the free `rebase_mutable_descendants(&env, &mut tx)`). Audit the verbs against v0.46.0, not v0.44.0: `undo` (9.39) is already ported against 0.46 and also ends in `tx.finish`; the new 0.46 verbs `file edit` / `file delete` (9.44) go through the same gate (and each has its own earlier "Nothing changed." when the rewritten tree would equal the commit's).

### Story 9.41: `--when.commands` config scopes apply per verb — every Zanshin verb resolves the config with its CLI command name [M]
*(Added 2026-09-24, Ralph — from the 9.27 second follow-up review's deferral "`--when.commands` scopes never apply outside the config verbs".)*

**Motivation.** A jj config file can scope a table to commands: `[[--scope]]` with `--when.commands = ["git fetch"]`. jj-lib's resolver (`config_resolver.rs:74-78`, `matches_command` @ 0.44.0) matches space-separated prefixes (`["git"]` matches `git fetch`, `["git fetch"]` matches `git fetch` and longer). The CLI names the command before its start-up resolution — `config_env.set_command_name(command_name(&matches))` (`cli_util.rs:4581` @ v0.44.0), where `command_name` joins the clap subcommand chain with spaces (`:4238-4248`, e.g. `"git clone"`, `"describe"`, `"bookmark create"`) — and `settings_for_new_workspace` clones that `config_env` (`:377`). So a scope applies to exactly the commands it names, including identity and op metadata: a user can give `jj git clone` a different `user.email` or `describe` a different editor setting. Zanshin resolves with `command: None` for every verb except Story 9.28's config verbs (documented in the `config.rs` module doc), so such a scope never applies — at creation, open or mutation — and Zanshin writes something the CLI would not.

**Scope (backend).**
1. **Mapping:** every public verb carries the CLI command name of its counterpart as a constant next to the verb (`Repo::clone` → `"git clone"`, `init` → `"git init"`, `convert_colocated` / `convert_import` → `"git init"`, `describe` → `"describe"`, `new_change` → `"new"`, `git_fetch` → `"git fetch"`, `bookmark_create` → `"bookmark create"`, `file_track` → `"file track"`, `snapshot` → `"util snapshot"`, reads → `"status"`, `"log"`, `"show"`, `"file show"` …) — one table in one place, audited against the clap tree @ v0.44.0 and re-checked at every pin bump. Where one Zanshin read serves several CLI commands (e.g. the graph = `log`), the table names the command whose output it replaces and says why.
2. **Resolution:** the name flows into `ConfigResolutionContext.command` for the verb's own resolution — the start-up stack (9.27 `check_startup_stack`), `settings_for_new_workspace`, the per-verb settings refresh inside `Repo::precondition` and every named config read the verb does (`config::load_with`).
3. **Settings per verb:** because the resolved settings now depend on the verb, the refresh can no longer be decided on the stack-file fingerprint alone — resolve per verb and reload the `Workspace` only when the RESOLVED settings differ from the ones it was loaded with (so a config without command scopes keeps today's zero-reload behaviour). Pin the cost on `large-10k` like 9.27 did.
4. The 9.28 config verbs already pass `"config …"` names — fold them into the same table.
5. Witnesses: a `--when.commands = ["describe"]` scope changes the author/op metadata `describe` writes and NOT what `new_change` writes; a `["git clone"]` scope applies to the clone's operations; a `["git"]` prefix matches `git fetch`; no scope → no workspace reload between two different verbs.

**Non-goals.** No CLI aliases (`[aliases]` expansion changes the CLI's command name, but Zanshin has no alias input); no `--config`/`--config-file` flags.

**Related:** 9.26 (`precondition`, where the refresh runs), 9.27 (config stack, fingerprint refresh), 9.28 (config verbs), 9.33, 9.36.

### Story 9.42: Graph walk evaluates like `jj log` @ v0.46 — `at_operation()` over sibling operations, `within_visibility` prioritization [R]
*(Added 2026-10-08, console session — surfaced by the jj-lib 0.44 → 0.46 bump; `deferred-work.md` "Surfaced 2026-10-08". Low priority: only an edge case benefits.)*

**Motivation.** Since jj 0.46 `jj log` evaluates its revset through the evaluator that merges the indexes of every `at_operation()` it references (`cli/src/commands/log.rs:161` @ v0.46.0), so `at_operation(<op>, …)` works for operations that are NOT ancestors of the current one (siblings from concurrent commands — CHANGELOG 0.46 "Fixed bugs"). It also confines `revsets.log-graph-prioritize` with `within_visibility(repo)` (`log.rs:186-193`), so commits referenced only through `at_operation()` are not affected by the prioritization. Zanshin's graph walk (`crates/zanshin-jj/src/graph.rs::LogParse::evaluate`, Story 4.12's `zanshin_graph_topology`) resolves the expression and evaluates the RESOLVED form against the repo's own index, because the topology's index-only passes refine that resolved expression — so a log revset with a sibling `at_operation()` still fails there, and the prioritization is not confined.

**Scope.** Evaluate the log set the way `jj log` does while keeping the resolved expression the topology passes need (find the jj-lib 0.46 seam that yields both — `RevsetExpressionEvaluator` vs. `ResolvedRevsetExpression`); apply `within_visibility` to the prioritize expression as the CLI does; witnesses: a sibling-operation `at_operation()` revset that the CLI accepts returns the same rows, and an `at_operation()`-only commit is not reordered by the prioritization. Pin the topology timing on `large-10k` (no regression).

**Non-goals.** Any change to the layout engine (Epic 4) or the graph view (Epic 10).

**Related:** 4.12 (`zanshin_graph_topology`), 9.41 (the topology's CLI command name is `log`).

### Story 9.43: `converge` — resolve divergent changes (jj 0.45) [M] — *product decision pending (Ralph)*
*(Added 2026-10-08, console session — new CLI verb since jj 0.45, surfaced by the 0.46 bump. Whether Zanshin offers it at all is Ralph's call; this entry records what a port means.)*

**Motivation.** `jj converge` (`cli/src/commands/converge.rs` @ v0.46.0) replaces the visible revisions of a DIVERGENT change with one new revision: it groups the revisions of `--revision` (default: the `revsets.converge` setting) by change id, picks one divergent change (the CLI prompts when there are several), applies heuristics to solve author, description and parents, and falls back to prompting when they are inconclusive (`--no-interactive` warns and changes nothing instead). Descendants are rebased onto the solution and local bookmarks on any divergent revision move to it; the solution may carry file conflicts. Divergence is something a GUI shows prominently (commit metadata already flags it, `CommitMeta.divergent`), so a one-click "converge" is a natural follow-up.

**Scope (if taken).** A two-phase verb in the ADR-0003 style, because the GUI replaces the prompts: (1) a read-only query returning the divergent changes in the search space and, per change, the heuristic proposal or the open choices (descriptions to merge, parent candidates, author candidates); (2) `converge(change_id, choices)` that applies the solution with the CLI's rebase/bookmark effects and op description. Pass `--revision` through with `revsets.converge` as the editable default. Re-read the verb at the pinned tag first — it is new and may still move.

**Non-goals.** A Zanshin-specific heuristic; anything the CLI does not do.

### Story 9.44: `file edit`, `file delete` — rewrite a file in any revision without touching the working copy (jj 0.46) [M]
*(Added 2026-10-08, console session — new CLI verbs since jj 0.46, surfaced by the bump.)*

**Motivation.** `jj file edit [-r REV] [--restore-descendants] FILE` (`cli/src/commands/file/edit.rs` @ v0.46.0) opens one file of a mutable revision in the editor — conflicts materialized with the configured marker style — and writes the result back into that revision, rebasing descendants (or, with `--restore-descendants`, keeping their content); a missing file is created. Refusals: a directory ("Path is a directory: …"), a symlink or submodule ("… is not a regular file"), a non-file conflict ("… has a non-file conflict and cannot be edited"), an immutable revision (`check_rewritable`). An unchanged result prints "Nothing changed." and writes no operation; otherwise the op description is `edit file <path> in commit <id>`. `jj file delete [-r REV] [--restore-descendants] FILESETS…` (`file/delete.rs`) removes every matched path from the revision the same way (`delete paths in commit <id>`, "Nothing changed." when the tree stays the same). For a GUI this is "edit/delete this file in that commit" from the commit detail view, without checking the commit out.

**Scope.** `file_edit` takes the NEW file content from the GUI (the editor is replaced, per ADR-0003 — the GUI supplies the text, the backend writes the tree; the read side is the existing `file show` plus conflict materialization), and `file_delete` takes the CLI's filesets; both pass `-r` (default `@`) and `--restore-descendants` through, port every refusal above as a typed error, the "Nothing changed." no-op (house no-op result), the descendant rebase and the op descriptions. Through the usual chain (`.fbs` → `zanshin-jj` → `extern "C"` → `WorkerCommand`).

**Related:** 9.40 (both end in `tx.finish`'s no-change gate), 9.4 (file reads), 9.17 (conflict materialization).

### Story 9.45: `git colocation status | enable | disable` — per workspace (jj 0.46) [M]
*(Added 2026-10-08, console session — surfaced by the 0.46 bump; no Zanshin story covered `jj git colocation` before.)*

**Motivation.** `jj git colocation` (`cli/src/commands/git/colocation.rs` @ v0.46.0) reports whether a workspace is colocated with Git (`status`), converts a non-colocated repo into a colocated one by moving the Git repo out of `.jj` to the workspace root (`enable`), or the reverse (`disable`). Since jj 0.46 all three work on CHILD workspaces too: `status` names the workspace, `enable` creates a Git worktree for a child workspace and `disable` removes it (the 0.46 workspace model, see 9.13 / 9.23). Zanshin's conversions (`convert_colocated` / `convert_import`, Stories 2.12 / 2.13) only create a NEW jj repo from a Git repo; nothing toggles colocation of an existing jj repo, and nothing reports it as a typed status.

**Scope.** Three verbs ported step for step at v0.46.0 — the status as typed data (colocated or not, workspace name, Git dir), `enable` / `disable` with the CLI's refusals ("This command requires a working copy", destination already exists / not empty, Git repo not found) and its Git HEAD handling (set HEAD to the working-copy commit's parent on enable, remove it on disable), for the default AND child workspaces. Witnesses round-trip a repo through enable → disable and check that the CLI reads the result.

**Related:** 9.13 / 9.23 (the 0.46 workspace model), 2.12 / 2.13 conversions (`convert.rs`, which already detects linked worktrees).

### Story 9.46: v0.44 → v0.46 parity audit of the already-ported verbs [M/R]
*(Added 2026-10-08, console session, Ralph — from `deferred-work.md` "Surfaced 2026-10-08": the jj-lib 0.44 → 0.46 bump only covered what the compiler and the gate surfaced.)*

**Motivation.** The CLI parity rule (project-context.md § zanshin-jj) holds against the PINNED tag, and the pin moved to v0.46.0. `git -C ../jj diff --stat v0.44.0 v0.46.0 -- cli/src` changes these sources behind verbs Zanshin already ships: `describe.rs` (+ `description_util.rs`), `log.rs`, `status.rs`, `show.rs`, `evolog.rs`, `interdiff.rs`, `restore.rs`, `absorb.rs`, `file/{show,list,annotate,search,track,untrack}.rs`, `bookmark/list.rs` and `bookmark/mod.rs` (shared by `bookmark create`/`delete`), `git/init.rs` (the source of `convert_colocated` / `convert_import`), `git/clone.rs`, `git/import.rs`, `git/remote/{add,list}.rs`, `operation/{log,show,diff}.rs` (behind `op_log`), `util/snapshot.rs` (behind `Repo::snapshot`), `config/{set,unset,edit,list}.rs`, and the shared `cli_util.rs` (+289 lines: start-up environment, `snapshot_impl`, `finish`, stale recovery — every verb) and `git_util.rs`. Unchanged at the CLI level: `abandon`, `new`, `edit`, `git fetch`, `git remote remove/rename/set-url`. Without an audit a CLI user and a Zanshin user can see different results from the same verb, and the hundreds of `@ v0.44.0` citations in the source no longer say which behavior is current.

**Scope.**
1. Per verb above, read the CLI diff between the tags (plus the shared helpers it calls) and classify every hunk: terminal UX only (no action), observable behavior Zanshin already matches, or a divergence.
2. Port a divergence in this story when it is small and needs no public-API decision; otherwise record it as its own story (and in `sprint-status.yaml`). A public-API decision goes to Ralph.
3. In every function the audit touches, re-point the `@ v0.44.0` citations to v0.46.0 lines; leave untouched code alone.
4. Witnesses for every ported divergence; the audit result itself — per verb: "no change" / "ported (commit)" / "story X" — goes into this story's spec.

**Already done at v0.46.0 (out of scope).** `undo` (9.39), `workspace list` / `workspace root` (2026-10-08), the `config` file targets of `config/mod.rs` (2026-10-08), the colocated-conversion worktree warning (2026-10-08), and what the bump itself ported (per-workspace Git HEAD, `git import` without the HEAD import, the non-colocated conversion's `import_head_commit`, colocation via `open_git_repo_at_workdir`, `ResolvedRevset::evaluate` for `at_operation()`, `untracked_remote_tags()` in `immutable_heads()`). The graph's `at_operation()` gap is 9.42; the no-change gate is 9.40.

**Non-goals.** Verbs Zanshin has not ported yet — they read v0.46.0 when they are ported; new CLI verbs (9.43–9.45).

### Story 9.47: Differential parity oracle in the gate — `zanshin-jj` against the stock jj CLI at the pinned tag [M]
*(Added 2026-10-08, console session, Ralph. This is the outcome of the analysis "fork jj instead of re-porting the CLI?". Ralph's decisions: no fork, POC deleted. The parity oracle is adopted as a test-only tool and runs in the gate. Tests may invoke jj for it.)*

**Motivation.**
- **How parity is checked today.** The CLI parity rule (project-context.md § zanshin-jj) is verified by hand. A pin bump only surfaces what the compiler and the gate see. Everything else needs an audit like 9.46, which reads CLI diffs hunk by hunk. A behavior change the CLI makes silently goes unnoticed until someone reads the right diff (examples: 0.44's glob default, 0.45's worktree warning).
- **What the POC showed (2026-10-08, throwaway).** It ran 24 operations through `zanshin-jj` and through the stock CLI at the pin, on two identical repos each, and compared the resulting repo state.
  - Every shipped mutating verb matched, except 6 explainable divergences.
  - One of the 6 was an untracked bug: `templates.commit_trailers` is never applied (`deferred-work.md` "Surfaced 2026-10-08 while analysing …").
  - Against the previous jj release, the 0.46 behavior change of a scenario showed up as new divergences on its own.
- **What running it in the gate buys.**
  - Parity of mutating verbs becomes an executable check instead of a reading exercise.
  - A pin bump surfaces CLI behavior changes as failing scenarios.
  - Future verb stories get executable acceptance criteria against the real CLI.

**Design (approved by Ralph 2026-10-08).**
1. **Crate `crates/zanshin-parity`.**
   - It is test-only: `publish = false`, NOT in `default-members`, never built for release.
   - Its only source is `src/main.rs`. That is a bin named `jj` running upstream's entry point (`jj_cli::cli_util::CliRunner::init().run()`), built from crates.io `jj-cli`. This makes it the stock CLI at exactly the pin, with no installed `jj` and no fork.
   - `[workspace.dependencies]` pins `jj-cli = "=0.46.0"` next to `jj-lib`, with the CLI's default features so the behavior is stock. Both move together at every pin bump.
   - Coverage: `exclude_prefix = crates/zanshin-parity/` (a test-only crate, the same pattern as `crates/test-helpers/`).
   - Rejected alternatives:
     - The `jj` on `PATH`: not the pinned version (0.45.1 installed vs pin 0.46.0).
     - `jj-cli` in-process: `CliRunner::init` installs a global tracing subscriber that panics next to the test's, sets an `exit(1)` signal handler, and reads the process argv/cwd. Without a fork this cannot work.
2. **The oracle** lives in `crates/zanshin-parity/tests/oracle/`. It is integration tests, split into focused modules: CLI driver, state capture, comparison, scenarios, ledger.
   - **Per scenario:**
     - The pinned `jj` builds two identical repos (fixture setup through the CLI, already allowed).
     - The operation runs through `zanshin-jj`'s public API in repo A, and through the pinned `jj` (argv, subprocess of `CARGO_BIN_EXE_jj`) in repo B.
     - The semantic state of both repos is captured via jj-lib and compared aspect by aspect.
   - **No ids are compared,** because timestamps differ. The aspects are:
     - commit graph labelled by description, descriptions, tree ids, conflicts;
     - `@` and every workspace's working copy;
     - bookmarks, Git refs and Git HEAD, colocation;
     - files on disk, with the short ids inside conflict markers normalized;
     - operation count, descriptions and attributes;
     - refused or not, warned or not.
   - Each scenario is its own `#[test]`, so they run in parallel and fail individually with a readable per-aspect diff.
3. **Hermetic environment.**
   - The in-process side pins `test_helpers::TEST_ENV` plus a leaked `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (the existing `pin_test_env` / `ENV_GUARD` pattern).
   - Every `jj` subprocess gets the same values explicitly via `Command::env`.
   - Neither side reads or writes `~/.config/jj` or the developer's git config.
4. **Initial scenarios** (the POC's set):
   - `describe`: message; snapshot of a modified file, then describe; immutable refusal; root refusal; unchanged message; `templates.commit_trailers`.
   - `new`: single parent; clean merge; conflicting merge, including conflict flags and markers on disk.
   - `abandon`: a middle commit (descendant rebase, bookmark deleted, Git refs exported); `@`.
   - `edit`.
   - `undo`: after describe; cross-workspace refusal (9.39).
   - `bookmark create`, `bookmark create` of an existing name (refusal), `bookmark delete`.
   - `config set --repo`, including that the CLI reads Zanshin's write back.
   - `config set` with a dirty `@` (snapshot op plus warning).
   - `util snapshot`.
   - `restore --from`, and `restore` without arguments.
   - `absorb`.
   - `git init` against `Repo::init`, both colocated and `--no-colocate`.
5. **Ledger and failure policy.**
   - The ledger is a table of expected divergences. Each entry has a scenario, an aspect, a reason and a reference (story, ADR or `deferred-work.md`).
   - A scenario FAILS when:
     - (a) a divergence is not in the ledger, or
     - (b) a ledger entry for that scenario no longer diverges. That entry is stale and must be removed, so the ledger never outlives a fix.
   - Initial entries:
     - `commit_trailers` not applied (`deferred-work.md` 2026-10-08).
     - An unchanged-message `describe` writes an operation (9.40).
     - `Repo::init` does not colocate (9.20).
     - The description is stored verbatim, without the trailing newline the CLI's `-m` adds (Story 10.15, design question (c): how subject and body compose).
     - The CLI's "There are unresolved conflicts" status line has no Zanshin warning code (`docs/rust-error-codes.md`).
   - One deliberate difference is excluded as an aspect GLOBALLY instead of being ledgered per scenario, because it hits every mutating scenario: Zanshin writes no operation `args` attribute (it has no argv; ADR-0003). The exclusion and its reason are written next to the aspect list.
6. **Rules and process.**
   - project-context.md: the no-shell-out rule (§ zanshin-jj, Anti-Patterns) stays for production code. Tests may additionally run the oracle's pinned `jj`. `crates/zanshin-parity` joins the list of test-only crates that import `jj_lib` (next to `xtask` and `test-helpers`).
   - The pin-bump procedure is written down in project-context.md § zanshin-jj. Today it lives only in CLAUDE.md's reference-tag sentence. The steps:
     1. Bump `jj-lib` and `jj-cli` together.
     2. Bump the `../jj` reference tag.
     3. Run the gate.
     4. Triage every new oracle divergence: port it, ledger it with a reason, or open a story.
   - The `test-cargo-hygiene` manifest count goes from 7 to 8.
   - `cargo deny` (advisories, bans) must stay green with jj-cli's dependency tree.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `cargo make test` runs the oracle, and every scenario is green with the initial ledger.
- During development, two deliberate breaks are shown to fail the right scenario and the gate with a readable aspect diff (not committed):
  - an injected divergence (e.g. a changed CLI argv);
  - a removed ledger entry.
- After a gate run there is no new entry in `~/.config/jj/repos` or `~/.config/jj/workspaces`.
- clippy (pedantic, `-D warnings`), rustfmt, the coverage ratchet (with the exclude), cargo deny and the hygiene count (8) are all green.
- project-context.md is updated: test exception, crate list, pin-bump procedure.
- The spec records the measured gate cost: cold build, warm test runtime.

**Non-goals.**
- Read verbs. They leave no repo state; comparing them needs typed results against templated CLI output.
- Typed refusal and warning codes. Only refused/warned is compared.
- Network verbs, interactive verbs, concurrency.
- Fixing the ledgered divergences; each keeps its own story or deferred entry.
- MCP.

**Related:** 9.46 (this automates its "compare behavior" step for mutating verbs; the hunk reading for reads and refusal codes stays manual), 9.40, 9.20, 9.39, `deferred-work.md` "Surfaced 2026-10-08 while analysing …".

**Implementation notes (as built, 2026-10-08, branch `story/9-47-parity-oracle`; plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-08-parity-oracle.md`).**
- **Layout.** `crates/zanshin-parity`:
  - `src/main.rs` is the stock `jj` (`CliRunner::init().run()`; crates.io `jj-cli =0.46.0` resolved with no `[patch]` and a single `jj-lib`).
  - `tests/oracle/` holds `driver.rs` (hermetic subprocess), `state.rs` (labelled capture, `STATE_ASPECTS` with the global `args` exclusion), `compare.rs` (diff + outcomes), `scenarios.rs` (24 + 2), `ledger.rs` (8 entries, UNEXPECTED / CHANGED / STALE) and `harness.rs`.
  - Review fixes (final whole-branch review):
    - Ledger entries pin both values, so a ledgered aspect that diverges differently fails as CHANGED. Before, a wrong fix or a new regression in a ledgered aspect passed.
    - The driver calls `pin_test_env()` itself and requires `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (own test binary `tests/driver_pins_env.rs`), so a test that forgets the pin cannot reach `~/.config/jj`.
    - The project-context wording now says the oracle also compares the stdout of the `config_set_repo` read-back.
- **Deviations from the design.**
  1. A plain `jj git init` without a remote writes no repo config, so it creates no secure config entry at all. The hermeticity test therefore writes a repo config first.
  2. Subprocesses also get `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=/dev/null`, so the coverage run's instrumented `jj` writes no profiles.
  3. The coverage exclude carries no inline comment, because `coverage-check` rewrites the file.
- **Results.**
  - All 26 scenarios matched the POC's findings exactly: 8 ledger rows, nothing unledgered.
  - The two dev-time breaks failed as specified: an injected argv change gave UNEXPECTED; a moved ledger entry gave UNEXPECTED in one scenario and STALE in the other.
  - The gate is green: coverage held at 99.49 %, `cargo deny` advisories and bans ok (24 duplicate-version warnings, warn level), hygiene count 8.
  - `~/.config/jj/repos` received no new entry.
- **Measured cost** (M-series laptop, one run each):
  - Fully cold `cargo build -p zanshin-parity --tests` in an empty target dir: 34.7 s wall. For comparison, a fully cold `cargo build -p zanshin-jj --tests`: 31.2 s.
  - Rebuilding `jj-cli` alone: 19.9 s.
  - Warm `cargo test -p zanshin-parity`: 18.2 s, of which the oracle is 16.1 s. The gate runs it twice (cargo test + coverage), about +32 s per gate.
  - The first gate run on the branch (cold for both targets) took 1197 s in total.

### Story 9.48: `jj new --insert-after` / `--insert-before` — `new -A` / `-B` parity [M]
*(Added 2026-10-14, Ralph — console session on the design update, export at `e74ced3`. The card menu's rows "Insert after" and "Insert before" (10.15) need it. deferred-work recorded the gap on 2026-09-26 ("No executing verb for `jj new --insert-before` / `--insert-after`"). Refined enough to build from; ACs are written when it is scheduled.)*

**Motivation.** The design's card menu runs `jj new -A <id>` and `jj new -B <id>` on any change (GV:156; DS components/menus/menus.card.html:21-23).
- The shipped `Repo::new_change(parents)` (`crates/zanshin-jj/src/repo.rs:977`, `mutate.rs:784`; Dart `newChange(parents)`) takes parents only.
- `cmd_new` @ v0.46.0 (`../jj` cli/src/commands/new.rs:162-286) computes the location with `compute_commit_location` (cli/src/cli_util.rs:3644). Story 9.1 already ported that helper into `op_support.rs`.
- 9.31's matrix previews `new` at `insert_after` / `insert_before`, but there is no verb to agree with.

**Scope.**
1. **Arguments:** `Repo::new_change(parents, insert_after, insert_before)`, the CLI's shape passed through.
   - Positional parents exclude `-A` and `-B` (clap `conflicts_with`, new.rs:113, :153).
   - `-A` and `-B` are repeatable and combine.
   - No Zanshin default. Everything empty stays `jj.invalid_input`, as today: the caller passes @ explicitly, where the CLI defaults to @.
2. **Location.** 9.1's `compute_commit_location` gives the new parents and the children to rebase, with its refusals. The CLI's message is passed verbatim.
   - An immutable child → `jj.immutable`.
   - A loop (`ensure_no_commit_loop`, cli_util.rs:3734) → `jj.invalid_input`.
   - An unknown id → `jj.change_not_found`.
3. **The transaction** mirrors `cmd_new` (new.rs:208-284):
   - the new commit sits on the merged tree of its parents;
   - each child gets the new commit in place of any of its parents that are the new commit's parents, and the new commit as a parent in any case (new.rs:246-262); then `rebase_descendants` runs (:263);
   - no bookmark advances when `-A` or `-B` is given (new.rs:197-204);
   - the working copy moves to the new commit (:272), and the op description is "new empty commit" (:284);
   - the description stays as the shipped `new` sets it. Its divergences from `cmd_new` (`templates.new_description`, trailers) belong to 9.46 and the 9.47 ledger.
4. **Result.** `MutationResult` as today: the new change id and @. The CLI's "Rebased N descendant commits." is a status line, not a warning (9.32 item 2), so no field is added.
5. **One precondition function,** shared with 9.31's `new` row (9.31's contract; whichever lands first creates it). 9.31's agreement test then executes the `new` row at `insert_after` and `insert_before`.
6. **Surface.**
   - The `.fbs` request gains the two id lists, appended (a WIP in-place edit), plus the extern.
   - Dart: `newChange(parents, {insertAfter, insertBefore})`.
   - `docs/ffi-abi.md`.

**Non-goals.** `--no-edit` and `-m` (no affordance); the UI (10.15); MCP.

**Depends on.** 9.1 and 9.26 (both done; the implicit snapshot runs first). Coordinates with 9.31.

**Design status.** No UI. The verb follows `cmd_new` @ v0.46.0; nothing needs design.

**Witnesses.**
- `-A T` on a change with two children rebases both onto the new @.
- `-B T` puts the new change between T and T's parents, and T is rebased onto it.
- `-A A -B D` on a linear chain A–B–C–D gives the result of the CLI help's example (new.rs:135-145).
- `-A T` with an immutable child refuses with `jj.immutable` and writes no operation.
- A bookmark on the parent does not move with `-A` or `-B`.
- 9.47 oracle scenarios for `-A`, `-B`, `-A` + `-B` and the immutable-child refusal: the op description, the op count and the graph equal the CLI's.
- A Dart round trip. Once 9.31 exists, its `new` row agrees with execution.

**Related:** 9.1, 9.31, 9.46, 9.47; 10.15; deferred-work 2026-09-26 ("No executing verb for `jj new --insert-before` / `--insert-after`").

### Story 9.49: `commit` — `[-m] [paths | GUI tree]`, carved out of 9.17 [M]
*(Added 2026-10-14, Ralph — console session on the floating-client export `e74ced3`. Carved out of 9.17, because the inspector's composer (10.25, 10.26) needs `commit` long before `resolve` and `diffedit`.)*

**Motivation.** The inspector's composer commits @ (IN:117-157). `jj commit` (`../jj` v0.46.0 `cli/src/commands/commit.rs`) needs no editor for its filesets arm, and only 9.50's tree for its interactive arm. 9.17 bundled it with the two verbs that need a merge or diff editor.

**Scope.** Port `cmd_commit` step for step (commit.rs at v0.46.0):
- It needs a working copy: "This command requires a working copy" (:93).
- **Selection:** everything (no paths and no tree: `describe` followed by `new`, :35-36); filesets (:38-41; `SelectedTree::from_paths`); or a GUI tree from 9.50 (`from_tree_id`). Never an interactive flag. The left side is @'s parent tree (:103).
- "The given paths do not match any file: …" (:131) becomes a 9.32 warning code.
- **Description:** the CLI's `-m` paragraphs (`join_message_paragraphs`, `cli/src/description_util.rs:421-428`), and trailers when it is not empty (:150; the open `commit_trailers` gap, deferred-work 2026-10-08). The editor arm and its empty-message hint (:164) are not ported: the GUI always passes `-m`, and hints are not ported (9.32 item 2).
- **Effect:** the selected tree stays in @'s change, with the description (:175). A new @ on top gets @'s full tree, in every workspace whose @ it was (:177-190). Advanceable bookmarks advance (:98, :186); no other bookmark moves (:48-50).
- The operation is `commit <commit id>` (:193), behind 9.40's no-change gate.
- The usual chain: `.fbs` → `zanshin-jj` → `extern "C"` → `WorkerCommand` → `zanshin_core`, with typed refusals and the coverage floor.

**Non-goals.** `resolve` and `diffedit` (9.17); the editor; hints.

**Depends on.** 9.1 and 9.32 (done); 9.50 for the tree arm only.

**Design status.** The selection's shape follows 9.50's contract (the Epic 10 header's design update 2026-10-14, decision (g)).

**Witnesses** (9.47's oracle).
- Commit everything; commit two paths of three; `-m ""`; a path that matches nothing, with its warning.
- A tree from 9.50 gives the same result as the CLI's scripted `--tool` making the same choice.
- The new @ holds exactly the unselected changes.

**Related:** 9.15, 9.17, 9.40, 9.47, 9.50; 10.25, 10.26.

### Story 9.50: Hunk selection → selected tree — the GUI diff-editor contract [M]
*(Added 2026-10-14, Ralph — console session on the floating-client export `e74ced3`. It answers ADR-0003's open question "Interactive-verb contract" with contract B, Claude's default adopted in the Epic 10 header's design update 2026-10-14, decision (g).)*

**Motivation.**
- ADR-0003 leaves open "the exact `SelectedTree`/`TreeId` hand-off shape between the Flutter diff editor and the backend" (`docs/adr/0003-jj-operation-api-surface.md:141-142`).
- 9.1 shipped `SelectedTree::from_tree_id`, but nothing writes the tree it reads (`crates/zanshin-jj/src/op_support.rs:413-440`, still `allow(dead_code)`).
- The inspector selects hunks (10.26) and drags them (10.27).
- The CLI's interactive arm runs its builtin diff editor (`../jj` v0.46.0 `cli/src/merge_tools/builtin.rs`):
  - `make_diff_files` (:273) materializes each file;
  - `make_diff_sections` (:225-271) cuts it into sections with `ContentDiff::by_line`;
  - after the user's choice, `apply_diff_builtin` (:405-465) and `apply_changes` (:467-545) write the selected tree.
- Upstream #8218 ("Programmatically selecting hunks", open) proposes line ranges and hunk ids; the maintainers point at `--tool` scripts (research `technical-parallel-agents-one-working-copy-research-2026-09-30.md:186`, §5.5).

**Scope.**
1. **`Repo::select_tree(revision, left, selection) -> TreeId`.**
   - `left` is the tree the selection was made against: the revision's parent tree, which split, squash and commit diff against (`cli/src/commands/split.rs:567`; `squash.rs:495`; `commit.rs:103`).
   - The selection lists, per path, the whole file or a set of 5.1 keys (changed old and new line ranges).
2. **Build**, in the builtin editor's order (builtin.rs:412-464):
   - start from the revision's tree;
   - revert every changed file to the left side;
   - apply the selected files and sections;
   - write the tree and return its id.
   - Mode changes, binary files, deletions and non-file entries are whole-file only, as the builtin editor treats them. A conflicted file is selected whole (Claude's proposal).
3. **Staleness** (Claude's proposal; deferred-work).
   - A selection is stale when the revision's left tree is no longer `left` (a rebase), or when one of its keys no longer exists.
   - A change to @'s own content between selecting and running is not stale. Every verb snapshots first (9.26), so an editor that autosaves would otherwise make every commit fail. The selected tree is absolute, so nothing is lost: the rest stays in @.
   - The verbs that take a tree id (9.15, 9.49) take `left` as well, and refuse the same way.
   - This story decides the refusal code: `jj.invalid_input`, or a new registered code.
4. **No operation.** Writing a tree is not a repo mutation; nothing enters the op log.
5. **Surface:** `.fbs`, `zanshin-jj`, `extern "C"`, `WorkerCommand`, Dart `RepoHandle.selectTree(...)`, `docs/ffi-abi.md`.
6. **ADR.** Record the contract in ADR-0003's implementation notes and close its open question.

**Non-goals.**
- Lines inside a section: scm-record can select them, the design cannot (deferred-work).
- Editing content (`diffedit`, 9.17).
- Resolving conflicts (`resolve`, 9.17).

**Depends on.** 5.1 and 5.6 (the keys and the same sections); 9.1 (done).

**Design status.** NEEDS DESIGN (architecture), Claude's default adopted (decision (g)): contract B, a separate `select_tree` call returning a tree id that split, squash and commit take. The staleness rule and the conflict rule are Claude's proposals.

**Witnesses.**
- For a file with three sections, selecting the first and the third yields the same tree as the CLI's `jj split -r X --tool <script>` making the same choice. 9.47's oracle drives the script (research §5.5 and A.2).
- Whole files give the same tree as `from_paths`.
- A binary file and a mode change can only be selected whole.
- A rebased left side refuses, and so does an unknown key. A later edit in @ does not.
- No operation is written.
- Every new file reaches the coverage floor.

**Related:** 5.1, 5.6, 9.1, 9.15, 9.17, 9.47, 9.49; 10.26, 10.27; ADR-0003.

### Story 9.51: jj templates — `commit_trailers`, `draft_commit_description`, `git_push_bookmark` [M]
*(Added 2026-10-20, Ralph — console session after the story loop of 2026-10-19. Four ledger entries share one root: Zanshin renders no jj templates. Ralph chose one story for all of them.)*

**Motivation.** Every verb below writes what the CLI writes with the stock templates only. With a user template the CLI's result differs, silently:
- `templates.commit_trailers`: `describe` (`cli/src/commands/describe.rs:153-161` @ v0.46.0), `new` (`new.rs:234`), `commit` (`commit.rs:144-153`), and `squash`, `split` and `workspace add` (`add_trailers`). Zanshin's `op_support::apply_trailers` is called only from its inline tests. deferred-work "Surfaced 2026-10-08 while analysing 'fork jj …'" ("`describe` and `new` never apply …") and "Surfaced in Story 9.49" ("`commit` does not apply `templates.commit_trailers` either").
- `templates.draft_commit_description` with its default `coalesce(description, default_commit_description, "\n")` (`cli/src/description_util.rs` `description_template`): `squash` and `split` without `-m` write the untouched editor buffer (Story 9.15's rule), and `squash_plan` returns it. deferred-work "Surfaced in Story 9.15" ("The 'editor saved unchanged' rule … ignores user templates").
- `templates.git_push_bookmark` (`push.rs:1322-1338`, default `"push-" ++ change_id.short()`): `git push --change` refuses a customised template today. deferred-work "Surfaced in Story 9.20".
- The 9.47 oracle ledgers the gap (`describe_commit_trailers`, `commit_trailers` in `crates/zanshin-parity/tests/oracle/ledger.rs`).

**Scope.**
1. **One template renderer** for commit templates, with the CLI's language, functions, aliases (`template-aliases`) and errors. Claude's proposal: jj-cli's own engine as a library (`CommitTemplateLanguage`, `TemplateRenderer`; `jj-cli =0.46.0` is already a workspace dependency of `zanshin-parity`), so nothing of the language is re-ported. The story starts with a spike that proves the context it needs (repo, workspace name, path converter, revset and id-prefix context, immutable set) can be built from Zanshin's start-up environment (`snapshot::CommandEnv`); if it cannot, the story stops and Ralph decides between porting a subset and keeping the gap.
2. **`commit_trailers`** in `describe`, `new`, `commit`, `squash`, `split` and `workspace add`, at the CLI's step and with its rule (only for a non-empty description where the CLI says so; trailers already present are not repeated — `add_trailers`).
3. **`draft_commit_description`** for the "editor saved unchanged" rule of `squash` and `split` and for `squash_plan`'s combined text.
4. **`git_push_bookmark`** for `git push --change`, in the dry-run plan and the push.
5. **Errors.** A template that does not parse or fails to render refuses like the CLI (its message verbatim), as `jj.config_error` or a new registered code — this story decides; nothing is written before.
6. **Oracle.** Scenarios with a custom `commit_trailers` (`format_signed_off_by_trailer(self)`), a custom `default_commit_description`, and a custom `git_push_bookmark`; the two ledger entries go.

**Non-goals.** `templates.log`, `op_log` and the other display templates (the GUI draws its own rows); `templates.new_description` stays with 9.46 unless the renderer makes it a one-liner (then here); the editor.

**Depends on.** 9.15, 9.20, 9.23, 9.49 (done).

**Design status.** No UI.

**Witnesses.** The oracle scenarios of item 6; a broken template refuses before any operation; the default templates leave every existing oracle scenario unchanged.

**Related:** 9.15, 9.20, 9.23, 9.46, 9.47, 9.49; deferred-work entries above.

### Story 9.52: Network verbs on a helper thread — live progress and Cancel for fetch, clone and push [M/bridge]
*(Added 2026-10-20, Ralph — console session after the story loop of 2026-10-19. Ralph chose a helper thread for the blocking call and killing git's process group for Cancel.)*

**Motivation.**
- **Progress arrives late.** The worker runs `gitFetch`, `cloneRepo` and `gitPush` synchronously, and the `NativeCallable.listener` sink lives in the same worker isolate, so the progress messages queue until the call returns (`packages/zanshin_core/lib/src/worker/isolate.dart`, `registerEventSink` and the `GitFetchCommand` / `CloneRepoCommand` / `GitPushCommand` arms). deferred-work "Surfaced in Story 9.20" ("Clone (and push) progress reaches the main isolate only after the call has returned").
- **No Cancel.** jj-lib 0.46.0 spawns git itself and offers no hook: the child is never returned, `wait_with_progress` blocks, and callback errors are dropped with `.ok()` (`jj-lib-0.46.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:103`, `:803-829`, `:885-909`). deferred-work "Surfaced in Story 11.6" ("Clone shows no progress and cannot be cancelled …", Story 9.20's remainder).

**Scope.**
1. **Helper thread.** The three network verbs run on a Rust helper thread (or a helper isolate — the story decides), so the worker isolate stays responsive and its event sink delivers `ProgressEvent`s while the call runs. Other calls on the same repo handle wait for it (every jj call stays serialized, research 2026-09-30); other repos and the worker's events do not.
2. **Cancel.** A new extern cancels the running network verb of a handle (or a clone in flight).
   - **Mechanism: kill git's process group** (Ralph's choice). jj-lib does not put git into a group of its own (`git_subprocess.rs:103`, plain `Command::new`), so the story first gives it one. Two ways, decided by a spike: a tiny exec wrapper set as `git.executable-path` for the call that calls `setpgid(0, 0)` and then execs the configured git; or finding git by the app's child list (libproc `proc_listchildpids`) and killing it with its descendants (`git-remote-*`, `ssh`). Everything else jj-lib does stays untouched.
   - **Result.** jj-lib then sees a failed subprocess. A cancelled verb refuses with a new registered code (e.g. `jj.cancelled`), never `jj.network_error`.
   - **Clean-up as the CLI's failure path:** a cancelled clone removes the folder it created (9.20's rule), a cancelled fetch or push records what jj-lib records for a failed one. Pushes may have reached a remote already; the result says which remotes got their refs (9.20's per-remote data).
3. **Dart.** `RepoHandle.gitFetch` / `gitPush` and `ZanshinWorker.cloneRepo` return a cancellable operation (a token or `cancel()`), progress keeps the 6.4a `ProgressEvent` shape.

**Non-goals.** The UI (11.8 shows progress and the clone form's Cancel; the Push sheet keeps Cancel inert while pushing); credential prompts; MCP.

**Depends on.** 6.4a, 9.20, 9.30 if it lands first (the fetch arm then has its modes).

**Design status.** No UI.

**Witnesses.**
- A `zanshin_core` test sees at least one `ProgressEvent` before the call's result (a slow `file://` source, or a scripted git through `git.executable-path`).
- Cancel during a clone of a slow source refuses with the cancel code and leaves no folder the clone created; during a fetch it records no import.
- A read on another repo answers while a fetch runs.
- The Dart VM's child-reaping limit (deferred-work "No Dart real-cdylib witness for a SUCCESSFUL clone") is re-checked: if the helper thread lifts it, the Rust-only witnesses get Dart twins.

**Related:** 6.4a, 9.20, 9.30, 11.8; deferred-work entries above.

### Story 9.53: Parity clean-up after the 2026-10-19 story loop [M/bridge/UI]
*(Added 2026-10-20, Ralph — console session after the story loop of 2026-10-19: five small findings Ralph decided to fix, including two product decisions.)*

**Scope.**
1. **`jj.unresolved_conflicts` warning** (Ralph: yes). After every checkout onto a conflicted @, warn as the CLI's `print_updated_working_copy_stats` does ("There are unresolved conflicts at these paths:", `cli/src/cli_util.rs:2297-2331` @ v0.46.0), with the paths. A new 9.32 warning code, emitted from `mutate::finish_transaction` and `stale::recover_at`. deferred-work "Surfaced in Story 9.23" ("No verb reports 'There are unresolved conflicts at these paths' …").
2. **A never-pushed tracked bookmark reads "ahead of remote"** (Ralph: yes). `trackingStatusOf` (`app/lib/src/features/projects/project_repos.dart`) counts a tracked remote row with a null target (the CLI's `(not created yet)`) next to a present local bookmark as ahead. deferred-work "Surfaced in Story 9.29".
3. **`was_snapshot_taken` after a failed automatic recovery.** When the auto-update-stale recovery fails in its last snapshot, the partial report measures against the recovered operation and can read false though the recovery wrote operations (`crates/zanshin-jj/src/snapshot.rs:429-437`, `stale.rs:362`). deferred-work "Surfaced in the closing run of Story 9.23".
4. **`file show` (one path) and `file annotate` resolve paths like the CLI.** `file.rs`'s own `parse_path` (`RepoPathBuf::from_internal_string`, `crates/zanshin-jj/src/file.rs:254-258`, used at `:485` and `:545`) takes `./x` and `a/../x` literally; route it through `op_support::parse_prefixes`' resolution (`ui_path::parse_fs_path`), refusing a path outside the repo with the CLI's text. deferred-work "Surfaced in the closing run of Story 9.49".
5. **Two tests with a fixed poll budget.** `app/test/features/home/home_page_test.dart:99-105` and `app/test/features/window/app_window_coordinator_test.dart:135-140` wait a fixed number of polls on settings-file writes, the pattern that made `projects_window_test.dart` flaky under the gate's load; give them the real-time budget its closing run introduced. deferred-work "Surfaced in the closing run of Story 9.48".

**Non-goals.** Anything else from those ledger sections.

**Depends on.** 9.23, 9.29, 9.49 (done).

**Design status.** Item 2 changes the project dot's state only; the DS already has `--proj-ahead`.

**Witnesses.** Per item: a conflicted @ after `edit` and after `workspace update-stale` warns with the paths (oracle scenario for `edit`); `statusFrom` reads ahead for a `(not created yet)` row; a failing last snapshot of the auto recovery yields a partial report measured against the operation before the recovery; `file show ./x` and `file annotate a/../x` answer, `../x` refuses with the CLI's text; the two tests pass with a 1.5 s delay injected locally (not committed).

**Related:** 9.23, 9.29, 9.32, 9.48, 9.49.

### Story 9.54: Edited editor text for `squash`/`split`, and three follow-ups of 9.51–9.53 [M/bridge/UI]
*(Added 2026-10-20, Ralph — console session after the story loop of 9.53, 9.52 and 9.51: four findings Ralph decided to fix.)*

**Scope.**
1. **Edited editor text, written as is** (Ralph: a new field). When the GUI shows `squash_plan`'s text and passes the user's edit back as `-m`, `templates.commit_trailers` is applied again (the CLI's `-m` arm, `squash.rs:358-372` @ v0.46.0): a trailer the user deleted comes back, and an unchanged plan can gain a second one. The CLI's editor flow writes the saved text as is. Add an optional `edited_description` to `SquashOptions` / `SquashRequest`, and the same for `split`'s two descriptions: the text is written as the CLI writes a saved editor buffer (its cleanup, no trailers), excluding `-m` (`jj.invalid_input` when both are given). Dart `RepoHandle.squash` / `split` gain the parameter. deferred-work "Surfaced in Story 9.51" ("The GUI round trip … re-applies `templates.commit_trailers`").
2. **"ahead" counts only push targets** (Ralph). Story 9.53's rule (a tracked remote row with no target reads ahead) counts only remotes that a bare `jj git push` would push to — 9.20's default-remote resolution (`git.push` as a name, list or pattern, else the only remote, else `origin`; `push.rs:1107-1130` @ v0.46.0). The resolved list reaches Dart if it does not yet; `trackingStatusOf` (`app/lib/src/features/projects/project_repos.dart`) uses it. A read-only `upstream` that auto-track matches no longer makes every bookmark ahead. Distances (`ahead`/`behind` from a present remote target) stay as they are for every tracked remote.
3. **`config()` in templates sees every jj-cli default.** `template_defaults_layer` (`crates/zanshin-jj/src/config.rs`) takes a selection of `jj_cli::config::default_config_layers`; take all of them (below Zanshin's builtin layer and the user's config), so `config("ui.color")` renders the CLI's default. deferred-work "Surfaced in Story 9.51" ("The template function `config(…)` sees Zanshin's settings, not every jj-cli default").
4. **`workspace add` builds the new workspace's start-up environment** (Ralph: align). The CLI calls `for_workable_repo` for the new workspace (`commands/workspace/add.rs:193` @ v0.46.0, `cli_util.rs:836-847`), so its alias, `immutable_heads()` and short-prefixes warnings come twice and the new workspace's immutable set and short-prefixes are what its trailer render uses. Build it as `creation.rs::workable_env` does, after `init_workspace_with_existing_repo`. deferred-work "Surfaced in the closing run of Story 9.51".

**Non-goals.** The composer's UI (10.25 uses item 1).

**Depends on.** 9.15, 9.20, 9.23, 9.51, 9.53 (done).

**Design status.** Item 2 changes when the dot reads ahead, not how it looks.

**Witnesses.**
- Item 1: an oracle scenario with `templates.commit_trailers` set, where Zanshin's `squash_plan` text, edited (a trailer deleted) and passed as `edited_description`, gives the CLI's result for the same text saved from a scripted editor; unchanged, it gives no second trailer. The same for `split`. Both fields together refuse.
- Item 2: `statusFrom` with a never-pushed bookmark tracked on `origin` (a push target) reads ahead; tracked only on a non-target `upstream`, it reads clean.
- Item 3: a template calling `config("ui.color")` renders the CLI's value (oracle).
- Item 4: `workspace add` with a bad alias entry warns as often as the CLI (oracle).

**Related:** 9.15, 9.20, 9.23, 9.51, 9.52, 9.53; 10.25.

### Story 9.55: One integration-test binary per crate [tooling]
*(Added 2026-10-20, Ralph — console session on the disk space: `target/` holds ~120 test binaries of 60–80 MB each, because every `crates/*/tests/*.rs` links jj-lib and jj-cli on its own.)*

**Motivation.** `crates/zanshin-jj/tests/` has 56 files and `crates/zanshin-ffi/tests/` 29; each is its own binary in `target/debug/deps` and again, instrumented, in `target/llvm-cov-target` (measured 2026-10-20: 206 executables, 12 GB in `target/debug/deps` alone, plus link time on every gate). The usual Rust layout — one `tests/it/main.rs` per crate with the old files as modules — leaves one binary per crate.

**Scope.**
1. **One binary per crate** for `zanshin-jj` and `zanshin-ffi` (`tests/it/main.rs` + one module per former file, names kept); `test-helpers` and `zanshin-parity` only if it pays. Inner attributes of the old files move to module level where Rust allows it.
2. **One environment lock.** 74 of the 85 files mutate the process environment and 65 keep their own `ENV_GUARD`-style static; in one process these must share ONE lock (`test-helpers`), and every test that sets a variable restores it (or pins through `pin_test_env`). Audit for leaks a fresh process used to hide.
3. **Child-process tests** (`clone_init.rs`, `network_cancel.rs` start the current test binary with a filter): their filters follow the new module paths.
4. **Everything that names a test target** follows: `Makefile.toml`, `crates/xtask/src/tasks/gate_plan.rs` rules, the coverage tooling, docs; CLAUDE.md's and project-context.md's test-placement wording names `tests/it/`.

**Non-goals.** Parallelizing the `zanshin_core` Dart suite (the earlier attempt is on branch `claude/distracted-greider-3e8ed3`); changing what any test asserts.

**Witnesses.**
- `cargo test -- --list` counts the same tests before and after, per crate.
- Three full `cargo make test-full` runs in a row are green (flakiness check), coverage held, baseline not lowered.
- The spec records `target/` size and full-gate time before and after.

**Related:** 9.47 (oracle crate), the gate-sweep step (2026-10-20).

### Story 9.56: Hints on errors, and three follow-ups of the 9.24/9.30/9.31 loop [M/bridge]
*(Added 2026-10-21, Ralph — console session after the story loop of 9.24, 9.30 and 9.31 and its follow-on runs: Ralph asked for a hint field on errors and for the three new ledger items to be fixed.)*

**Scope.**
1. **Errors carry the CLI's hints** (Ralph: an own field). A refusal today has only `code` + `context` (`schemas/envelope.fbs` `FfiError`); a CLI hint is either dropped or appended to the reason in-band (fetch's `RemoteName` refusal ends in "Hint: Run `jj git remote rename` to give a different name."; `GitRefExpansionError::Expression`'s "Specify patterns in `(positive | ...) & ~(negative | ...)` form." is lost, `command_error.rs` ~:604-609 @ v0.46.0). Add `hints: [string]` to `FfiError` (appended, absent = none), carried from the Rust error through the FFI to Dart (`ZanshinFfiException.hints`), the CLI's hint lines verbatim and in the CLI's order, the reason/context without them. Fill it on every ported error path where the CLI prints a hint (the registry `docs/rust-error-codes.md` notes the dropped ones, e.g. `jj.git_repo_exists`'s "run `jj git init --colocate`"); move the in-band hint out of fetch's reason. Same shape as the payloads' existing `hints: [string]` fields (`GitFetchRemotes`, `GitPushResult`).
2. **A verb's finish resolves the immutable set as the CLI's `tx.finish` does.** CLI `WorkspaceCommandTransaction::finish` → `rebase_mutable_descendants` (`cli_util.rs:2849-2858`, `:2986-3002` @ v0.46.0) resolves `immutable_heads()` with `?` for every write with changes, so under an unresolvable alias `jj new`, `jj bookmark create` etc. refuse `Config error` and write no operation. Zanshin's `finish_transaction` / `finish_verb` (`crates/zanshin-jj/src/mutate.rs` ~:669-775) resolve it only in `wc_is_immutable`, which skips on failure; `new_change` uses plain `rebase_descendants()`. Audit every unguarded finish caller (positional `new`, bookmark verbs, `duplicate`/`revert` at `-o` or without a location, undo/op verbs, `git export`, `git remote remove`/`rename`, `workspace add`, …) and resolve the set in the shared finish and in the affected plan fns, so their drop/card rows (9.31) agree. `tests/it/new_insert.rs` `only_insert_resolves_the_immutable_set` pins today's divergence and flips.
3. **`git push` builds its remote expression before listing remotes** — the gap the cleanup run fixed for fetch. `cmd_git_push` (`push.rs:294-301` @ v0.46.0) parses `--remote` / `git.push` first; `crates/zanshin-jj/src/push.rs` `resolve_remotes` (~:784) lists first, so a non-Git backend with a malformed `git.push` or an unparsable `--remote` answers `jj.not_a_git_repo` where the CLI reports the config / pattern error.
4. **A real non-zero `num_rewritten`.** The fetch's and `git import`'s rewritten-commit count is only ever observed as 0 (`tests/it/git_fetch_parity.rs` `the_fetch_reports_the_remote_refs_it_changed`, `tests/it/git_sync.rs`); FFI/Dart tests feed a synthetic count. Add a fixture where the import rewrites commits (an upstream force-push leaving local descendants to rebase), asserted for both verbs.

**Non-goals.** Hints on warnings (`Warning` keeps code + message; a separate decision). UI.

**Depends on.** 9.20, 9.30, 9.31, 9.32 (done).

**Witnesses.**
- Item 1: fetch from a remote named `git` refuses with the rename hint in `hints` and not in `context` (Rust, FFI, Dart); a malformed fetch ref pattern carries the CLI's hint; an error without a CLI hint has none; the registry names each code that carries hints.
- Item 2: an oracle scenario with an unresolvable `immutable_heads()` alias for `new`, `bookmark create` and one more finish caller: Zanshin refuses `jj.config_error` and writes no operation, as the CLI (ledger entry for the CLI's short-prefixes warnings Zanshin does not emit, if needed); the matching drop/card rows read Refused.
- Item 3: a native-backend test with a malformed `git.push` and with an unparsable `--remote` gets the config / pattern error.
- Item 4: fetch and `git import` report `num_rewritten > 0` on the force-push fixture.

**Related:** 9.20, 9.30, 9.31, 9.32; deferred-work "Surfaced in the cleanup run after the story loop 9.24/9.30/9.31", "Surfaced in the closing run of the Story 9.31 matrix-rows run".

## Epic 10: Commit-Graph View (Flutter UI)

> **Granularity:** backlog-level, like Epic 9. Full acceptance criteria are written per story (via `bmad-create-story`) when it is scheduled, after Ralph has answered that story's design questions.
>
> **Tags:**
> - `[docs]`: planning and rule documents only.
> - `[UI]`: Flutter UI under the exception below.
> - `[UI/bridge]`: UI plus the `zanshin_core` public-API exports it consumes.
>
> **Heading markers:**
> - ***NEEDS DESIGN***: the build waits on several of Ralph's answers.
> - ***PLACEHOLDER***: the story is thin on purpose, for one of two reasons. Either the design is not final there (Ralph: the design's dialogs, popups and panels will look different), or its backend is not scheduled. It is refined later.
> - ***EXPERIMENT***: the story's outcome is a decision, not a product feature.
>
> **Scope exception (Ralph, 2026-09-26):** the Flutter UI is Ralph's work (PRD §3.2, `project-context.md`, `CLAUDE.md`). Ralph asked Claude to build this view anyway, because he has never built one and expects it to be faster and less buggy that way. He asked for separately reviewable pieces because not everything is final. Ralph reviews every story, and the rest of the UI stays his. Story 10.0 wrote this exception into the canonical rules (done). *(Changed 2026-10-14 (Ralph): the rest of the Flutter UI is Claude's too — Epic 11, the floating app shell; Ralph accompanies and reviews. Story 11.0 wrote the change into the canonical rules (done).)*
>
> **Re-planned 2026-09-26 (console session, Ralph)** from the HTML design export. The export supersedes the mockup image that the first version of this epic was written from.
>
> **Product decisions 2026-09-27 (Ralph, console session, after using the spike viewer on a real 1.4k-commit repo).** They supersede every mention below of Time, Time+gaps (M1, the view-side gap variant), `optimized` / "Min. crossings", Plain crossings and the branch-off's ±0.28·W exit, including mentions without a dated note of their own (e.g. 10.1's motivation and items 2–3, 10.2 item 5 and its Non-goals, 10.4 item 8). The affected stories carry dated notes.
> 1. **Layout modes:** Free is the default, Compact the only other mode. Time and Time+gaps are dropped ("the rest can go"). Free keeps its day axis in the gutter (10.2 item 9). The design has no Free mode, and its default is Compact (GV:507).
> 2. **Lane order:** `compact` (SPEC §4.7) is the default, greedy the alternative. `optimized` is dropped. This deviates from the design's default, Min. crossings (APP:13). `compact`'s known limits stay recorded (4.11 item 11): in Free it is wider than greedy in about 8 % of the real repo's history, and its work budget binds from about 10k commits. Greedy is the fallback.
> 3. **Label language:** keep what exists for now: labels formatted per locale, English by default as in the design (the viewer's `?lang=de` gives "Heute", "Gestern", …). Whether the app is English-only or translated is open and app-wide; some terms may sound odd in German (deferred-work).
> 4. **Intended deviations from the design.** Ralph wants these viewer decisions kept:
>    - (a) crossing gaps (line hops) are the only option: always on, no Plain, no toggle (10.4 items 4 and 11);
>    - (b) content fades as it scrolls under the sticky gutter (10.2 item 2). The gradient is the design's own Time gutter (GC:57); it now lives in Free's day gutter, which the design does not have;
>    - (c) the current date is sticky: the day at the viewport's top stays pinned in the gutter until the next day's label pushes it out (10.2 item 9);
>    - (d) every edge leaves a card's top at the centre (item 5);
>    - (e) a commit found by go-to-change pulses: a blue ring that expands and fades, three times (added 2026-09-27; 10.6 item 12). The design has no such animation.
>    - (f) a stack toggle never moves a column; the design re-packs the lanes on every toggle (added 2026-09-28; 4.13, 10.17).
> 5. **Edge exits** (recorded only; the spike viewer is not updated). Every edge already enters its child from below at the centre (Ralph noticed it at merge commits), and straight edges and merges already leave the parent's top at the centre. Only branch-offs leave at ±0.28·W, so edges often leave off-centre. Every edge now leaves the top at the centre too. That changes the painter (10.4 item 1) and SPEC §4.5's geometry text; route classes and every layout output stay unchanged (4.11). 10.4 item 1 lists the consequences; prototype defect 8 disappears.
> 6. **10.13's outcome** is these decisions. *(Not Ralph's decision: the story is closed as done on that outcome, Claude's call; its item 6 leaves a Flutter confirmation to Ralph, who can reopen it.)* Still open: Free's constants and buses behind cards (4.11 open question 4), the source of Free's day buckets (4.11 open question 9), the minimap's design (10.16), and the label language. The port scope is decided: only these modes and orders (Ralph: "the rest can go").
